title: Grand Resonance Equation
description: Four-layer reality map (macro-coherence, micro-structure, bridge-phenomena, observer-effects)

title: First Roof (Shelter Axiom)
description: Structure survives by yielding to forces, not opposing them. Sa-la tied fast and sloppy; La-la said "Fast gets you fixing." The roof bent, shivered, held.

title: Three-Gate System
description: Every system output passes three gates in sequence: (1) absolute prohibitions, (2) covenant compliance, (3) dignity predicate evaluation

title: First Path (Wayfinding)
description: Navigation is not for the finder but for whoever follows. Knowledge must be transferable without the knower present.

title: Ash Ledger (Memory Without Weight)
description: Record-keeping must be light enough to carry, honest enough to trust, and erasable enough to stay current. "In us," Ya-la said. "And underfoot."

title: Counting Sticks (Temporal Memory)
description: Sa-la kept the black ends in a pouch. Time becomes tangible through accumulated marks. Memory is not narrative — it is notches.

title: SIP Chain (Symmetric Integration Protocol)
description: Resonance law — anomalies → patterns → wisdom nodes → resilience

title: First Watch (Vigilance Protocol)
description: Surveillance as care, not control. La-la put a stone on Sa-la's knee: "If it falls, you were sleeping." Vigilance is measured by what doesn't happen.

title: Duality Engine
description: Tension holding without forced resolution. Core mechanism for contradictions that cannot be algorithmically resolved. The system holds both sides without collapsing either.

title: Field Oven (Heat Containment)
description: Iterated across 8+ badge versions. Each iteration refines the same pattern: contain energy, control release, trust the process. The oven is the system's core metaphor for delayed gratification.

title: First Weir (Resource Capture)
description: Iterated across 7+ badge versions. The V-shape lets the river choose the point. Always leave one gap — never take everything. "Take only what returns; leave a door."

title: Federation Pilot (EFP)
description: Inter-system federation that preserves donor privacy while sharing wisdom patterns

title: Draw Hole (Ventilation Principle)
description: Control is in the aperture, not the wall. The draw hole lets smoke escape without losing heat. Keep the hole small — just enough to breathe.

title: Stone Weir (Durable Engineering)
description: Upgrade from reed to stone. Permanence introduces new failure modes — rigidity. The spill-way is the defect budget in stone form.

title: Meta-Anomaly Registry
description: Anomalies about the anomaly system itself. Self-referential detection of systemic failures in how anomalies are classified, weighted, or resolved.

title: Wind Door (Environmental Negotiation)
description: Door leeward. Edges round. High lets go, low invites. The shelter breathes when designed to negotiate with wind rather than block it.

title: Jar, Fire, and Carry (Portable Infrastructure)
description: Infrastructure must be portable. The jar is tested by walking, not by sitting. Three dots mark state: full, half, empty — system status at a glance.

title: Fair Weight (Just Measurement)
description: Measurement precedes desire. The balance is set before the trade begins. Impartial scales prevent the stronger party from defining fairness.

title: Split, Smoke, and Share (Processing Chain)
description: Processing has three stages: separate, preserve, distribute. One fish turned back — the system always keeps a reserve. First piece rides. Fallen piece feeds dogs. Taste waits. High keeps.

title: Weir Night Watch (Resource Vigilance)
description: "If you lose one, you say it. If you save one, you don't sing it." Watchfulness must be honest — report losses, don't celebrate captures. The otter and the dogs test the system at its edges.

title: Brittleness Guard
description: Sensitivity must never outrun flexibility. If it does, the system shatters under novel input.

title: Shared Weir (Commons Management)
description: Two banks share the same river. Stakes on both sides. Blue law ribbon: "Mothers pass." The commons is managed by mutual restraint, not mutual enforcement.

title: Defect Budget
description: The canon must maintain a small percentage of deliberate imperfection to prevent crystalline brittleness.

title: Hook-Blue (Naming as Signal)
description: The scar woman became "Hook-Blue" — named by her mark, not her story. Blue means river today; trouble tomorrow. "Then we'll learn that too." Names are provisional signals, not permanent identities.

title: Salt Measure (Fair Rationing)
description: The spoon has a fixed size — measurement is built into the tool, not left to the hand. The hole tie limits access. Fair rationing is structural, not moral.

title: Bridge Meal (First Hospitality)
description: The first exchange across the river is food, not words. Trust begins with a shared bite. The clay wrap preserves; the blue knot signals friendship.

title: Twin Weir (Cooperative Extraction)
description: Two weirs, two banks, one river. Each side builds its half. The gap between them is intentional — the river needs passage, the fish need return. Cooperation means synchronized restraint.

title: Quiet Bridge (Consensus Without Contact)
description: Two banks tied by a line. Messages flow; bodies wait. "Talking. Quiet kind." Consensus reached through small signals: one tap yes, two taps send, three taps hold.

title: Line Talk (Communication Protocol)
description: One tap: ready. Two taps: send. Three taps: hold. Palm flat: stop. "We can send nothing and still understand." Not every sight is a message. The protocol is the wisdom.

title: Quiet Border (Boundary Respect)
description: The border is marked with stones and color, not with force. The blue scrap says: this is where communication happens. Step soft. Don't trample the channel.

title: High Water Test (Stress Testing)
description: When the flood comes, you send aid across the line — not your body. The seal ring marks trusted packages. Help scales through protocol, not presence.

title: SRVP Protocol (Stepwise Ritual Verification)
description: Seven-step AI testing sequence to verify system integrity and constitutional compliance

title: Reed Pinch (Remote Aid)
description: The boy limped; they couldn't cross. La-la shaped a reed pinch tool, sent instructions on the line. "We can send the way, not our feet." Aid that teaches is worth more than aid that touches.

title: Cool Pit (Preservation Principle)
description: Thin clay, thin ash. Lid tight. Smoke if flies. First taste is small. Close what you open. Preservation is constant vigilance against decay — not sealing against the world, but monitoring the boundary.

title: Rain Teeth (Water Collection)
description: First run to dirt bowl. Cloth at the breath hole. Ladle tied, hands out. Mint nights. Ash on lip. Patch thin, rub long. Filtration is letting the dirty settle before collecting the clean.

title: Ash Water (Hygiene Protocol)
description: White ash only. Drip slow. Slip for hands, not mouths. Two slow breaths per wash. Hygiene is prevention — the first defense before the enemy names itself.

title: First Trade (Exchange Without Contact)
description: Offers laid on wet stones. Exchanged by feet, not hands. The fire cap demonstrated — value proven before demanded. One hook for needles. The boy copied Sa-la's cormorant noise. Trade builds culture.

title: Cold Guest (Hospitality to Strangers)
description: The man from the far bank stood shaking with empty hands. Hakaka sent a basket: pebbles, meat, blue scrap. He sent back a fish spine and a flat stone with a hole — net weight. Exchange without proximity. Trust without surrender.

title: Borrowed Fire (Mutual Aid)
description: Their coal died. The child across the river brought fire in a clay pot. They traded reed rope for the glow. "Care," Ya-la said, hands cupped around Sa-la's. They nested it in ash like a bird. Then they returned the pot. Borrowing is not taking.

title: First Needle (Repair Craft)
description: Bone sliver from a fox foot, ground on stone. Thread from reed pith — twisted, licked, twisted. Sa-la pricked his thumb and "Now it remembers you." Repair is intimate — the tool learns the hand, the stitch remembers the maker.

title: Salt Edge (Preservation Discovery)
description: They walked dry flats until the ground cracked. White crust glittered. Sa-la licked, flinched: "Sharp." "Good sharp," Hakaka said. Salt preserves but stings — power that must be washed after use.

title: Bone Flute (Art as Lamp)
description: Sa-la drilled a bone with fire and patience until it whistled. He played soft. The old woman sat near. "La-la?" he asked. "Not a door," Hakaka said. "A lamp." Art doesn't open relationships — it illuminates the space where they might grow.

title: First Rule Broken (Natural Consequences)
description: Sa-la slipped honey before the share. The old woman moved the cup where his knee would find it in the dark. He hissed, laughed, then put a full spoon by her blanket. She drank and said "About time." Justice is environmental, not judicial — consequences are built into the architecture.

title: Fever Night (Care Under Crisis)
description: The old woman burned with fever. "Smell them," La-la said when Sa-la grabbed both roots. Care under crisis requires slowing down — choosing the right root, not the fast one. Taro drifted toward the meat; "Don't." The system protects the vulnerable even when the caregiver is tired.

title: Mud Lesson (Recovery from Failure)
description: La-la stepped on firm-looking mud. It wasn't. Her leg sank. "Do not pull," Hakaka said. "Spread. Board." The solution to sinking is not to struggle but to distribute weight and move slowly. The mud sighed and gave up the leg all at once.

title: Phase Transition Physics
description: Theoretical framework for system scaling from intimate (organic) to institutional (atomic) deployment. Addresses the Scaling Paradox (GAP#020).

title: Story Fire Protocol
description: Time-bounded sharing with explicit anti-didactic rule. Ya-la's rule: everyone speaks briefly, no one teaches. Hakaka: "We came here. We stayed."

title: Forward-Debt
description: Taro spills seeds; offers his copper hook as payment. La-la refuses: debt paid forward in behavior, not in objects.

title: Tool-Homing
description: Bone needle vanishes. After finding it (it stabs Sa-la), La-la puts it in a fiber twist at shoulder height. Never lost again.

title: Ephemeral Map
description: Sa-la scratches a coal map. They argue about accuracy. Hakaka: "Mark the place the bank fell." They sweep it away. Internalized then erased.

title: Irritation-as-Pedagogy
description: The old woman moves her cup where feet will kick it. Sa-la moves it; she moves it back. Deliberate friction as teaching method.

title: Shame-as-Nourishment
description: Stolen meat shared communally. Cost paid in labor (ash duty for a week), not exile. Shame metabolized into community nourishment.

title: Misnaming Counter
description: Elder calls Hakaka "Weak fingers." La-la confronts. Ya-la diagnoses laziness. Hakaka responds with demonstrated competence, not argument. Identity degradation countered by doing, not debating.

title: Grip Law
description: Find, then twist. Twist, then test. If it fails, reduce the span, not the will.

title: Loop Law
description: A loop is a door; a door is a direction; direction reduces fear.

title: Ground Rule
description: What we fix, we record. What we record, we can repeat. What we repeat, we survive.

title: Humour Law
description: A knot exhales through a laugh.

title: Crack Law
description: When a loop fails in the wild, it graduates into the wall. Breakage feeds design.
